draft.title: Limiting sums
card: A geometric series adds terms that multiply by a common ratio r each time. If r is between -1 and 1, the terms shrink towards 0.
When -1 < r < 1, the sum of the first n terms gets closer and closer to one number as n grows. This number is the limiting sum: S = a/(1 - r), where a is the first term.
If r is 1 or more, or -1 or less, the terms do not shrink to 0. The sum does not settle on a number, so there is no limiting sum.
Example: 12 + 6 + 3 + ... has a = 12 and r = 6/12 = 1/2. This is between -1 and 1, so S = 12 ÷ (1 - 1/2) = 12 ÷ 1/2 = 24.
draft.remember: Check r first. If -1 < r < 1, use S = a/(1 - r). If not, there is no limiting sum.

a.q: A geometric series has first term 18 and common ratio 1/3. What is its limiting sum?
a.why: Here -1 < r < 1, so S = 18 ÷ (1 - 1/3) = 18 ÷ 2/3 = 27. Using 18 ÷ 1/3 = 54 is tempting, but it forgets to subtract r from 1 first.
a.clue: Work out 1 - r before you divide.

b.q: Which of these geometric series has a limiting sum?
b.why: 8 - 4 + 2 - 1 has r = -4/8 = -1/2, which is between -1 and 1, so it has a limiting sum (16/3). The negative sign does not stop it. The others have r = 2, r = -1 and r = 1.1, and none of these is between -1 and 1.
b.clue: Check each r. A negative r can still work.
